history.summary: Sukh Mahal (Sukh Nivas Mahal) is a lakeside palace on the Jait Sagar (Sukh Sagar) lake built in 1773 (some sources 1776) by Rao Raja Vishnu Singh, under Diwan Sukhram, as a royal summer retreat; Rudyard Kipling is traditionally said to have stayed here. UNCERTAIN IDENTITY: no consulted source documents a Shiva temple named 'Sukh Mahal Shiva Temple'. The CSV name appears to be a misnomer conflating the palace with a shrine; a small Shiva shrine may exist in or near the complex (a generic 'Shiv Mandir' is listed near the lake on map services) but this is unverified - treat deities, festivals and opening hours below as provisional. Composite ticket (Rs 75) covers Sukh Mahal, Rani Ji ki Baori and the 84 Pillared Cenotaph.

name: Sukh Mahal Shiva Temple
town_description: Bundi, the 'City of Stepwells', is a historic Hadoti town in southeastern Rajasthan centred on the Taragarh Fort and the Garh Palace, famous for its ornate baoris (Rani Ji ki Baori), cenotaphs and lakes including Jait Sagar.

travel.railway: Bundi railway station (well connected on the Delhi-Mumbai route)
travel.road: NH-116A via Kota (42 km) or Jaipur; Sukh Mahal is ~3 km from the Bundi bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (also the Bundi Utsav season)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple hours unverified; the Sukh Mahal museum/compound is visited during daylight hours (typically around 9:30 AM-5:30 PM) - verify before visiting
